title: Solid electrolyte ionic conductivity extraction (one paper)

paper_in_scope.description: True if the paper reports at least one ionic conductivity of a solid Li/Na-ion conductor.

scope_note.description: One sentence on why the paper is or is not in scope.

material_as_written.description: Composition exactly as written in the paper, e.g. 'Li6.55Ge0.05La2.95Ca0.05Zr1.75Ta0.25O12' or 'LLZO-0.05Ca'.

dopants.description: Element symbols of intentional substituents, e.g. ['Ga','Ta']. Empty if undoped.

data_origin.description: literature_cited = a value the paper quotes from another paper. Still record it, but mark it.

synthesis_method.description: Short phrase, e.g. 'solid-state reaction', 'sol-gel', 'ball milling', 'spark plasma sintering'. null if not stated.

conductivity_value_as_reported.description: The number exactly as it appears in evidence_quote, without the unit, e.g. '9.95 x 10-4' or '1.2'. Copy character for character; do not tidy '10-4' into '10^-4'.

conductivity_unit_as_reported.description: The unit exactly as the paper writes it, e.g. 'S/cm', 'mS cm-1', 'S cm−1'.

unit_evidence_quote.description: null if the unit is inside evidence_quote. Otherwise (typical for table cells) a verbatim span that shows the unit, such as the column header or caption.

measurement_temperature_as_reported.description: Copied from the paper, e.g. '25 °C', 'room temperature', '300 K'. null if not stated anywhere.

measurement_temperature_C.description: Only if the paper gives a number. Do NOT convert 'room temperature' to 25; leave null.

evidence_quote.description: A verbatim span of the paper text (max ~300 characters) that contains conductivity_value_as_reported and, where possible, identifies the material. For a table, copy the whole row. Copy exactly; do not fix typos or spacing.

notes.description: Anything ambiguous. Empty string if none.
